task:
Implement the immutable V3 application release/deployment foundation on existing branch release/v3-application-foundation, created from current main 7102ec1cf706020ea8268edd595df6d5e52c0006. Read CLAUDE.md, README.md, docs/development/v3-application-stack-decision.md, docs/operations/infrastructure-status.md, docs/operations/operator-command-contexts.md, scripts/operator/README.md, the current chatgpt-ed-new-ops workflow and action scripts, apps/api Dockerfile/config/health/auth/OpenAPI routes, apps/web build/static fallback configuration, nginx boundaries, schema migration ledger, CI/action pinning conventions, and tests. Treat these first-hand production facts as authoritative: the V3 host is ed-finder-prod / nb79a3d.mevnode.com; PostgreSQL 18 and support containers are healthy; origin API health on 127.0.0.1:58080 returns 200/database connected from stale image edfinder-v3-api:phase4c-r5 with build_sha unknown; current origin lacks /openapi.json and /api/auth/*; no frontend index exists; public health is 503; public anonymous session responds; existing app containers are edfinder-v3-api, edfinder-v3-proxy and edfinder-v3-public-auth-edge; the host checkout is a historical branch and must not be used as a release artifact. A safe runtime-contract export was attempted and correctly failed closed because the old docker-compose.yml contains credentialed URIs and sensitive environment assignments. Do not weaken that scanner, export the old Compose, print secrets, or copy sensitive config off-host.

Build a production-grade, independently reviewable release foundation that can later deploy the final Svelte head without building or git-pulling on production. Prefer the smallest safe architecture compatible with the retained edge: an immutable API image plus an immutable nginx web/proxy image that serves apps/web adapter-static output and owns same-origin routing, while leaving edfinder-v3-public-auth-edge, PostgreSQL 18 and support/data containers untouched. Requirements:

1. Add a reproducible multi-stage apps/web production Dockerfile using the locked Node 24/pnpm 11/frozen lock policy, producing only the static Svelte build and a minimal non-root or otherwise hardened nginx runtime. Add a dedicated nginx config with exact boundaries: /api/*, exact /openapi.json and numeric /s/{id64} proxy to FastAPI; every other static/application route stays with the Svelte build and receives the deliberate SPA fallback. Preserve correct GET/HEAD/static caching, query strings, malformed/encoded-path fail-closed behaviour, security headers, and no backend catch-all.
2. Harden the API image for immutable provenance. Inject exact 40-hex BUILD_SHA and a host-neutral APP_VERSION at build/runtime, make /api/health report them, and reject production release identity unknown. Do not bundle frontend output into the API image. Add *_FILE handling or an equivalently testable mounted-secret mechanism for sensitive API settings needed by the current runtime, at minimum database URL, Redis/Valkey URL, admin token, Frontier client secret and telemetry DSN, while preserving existing env compatibility outside production. Never make a secret a frontend build input.
3. Add a dedicated V3 production runtime authority under a clearly named deploy/operations directory; do not reuse root docker-compose.yml. It must reference images by immutable digest or exact content identity supplied by a release manifest, contain no inline secret values, retain the existing external PostgreSQL/support services rather than define/recreate them, and recreate only the selected V3 application services. Use the real retained container names/edge contract where required. Because the old Compose cannot be exported, implement fail-closed host-side topology discovery from docker inspect that records only non-secret network/port/mount/container metadata and never logs environment values. Require exact expected host/FQDN and healthy PostgreSQL/support prerequisites.
4. Define a versioned release-manifest schema and generator/validator. Record exact Git SHA, API and web image content IDs/digests, Dockerfile/lock/config hashes, SQL migration-manifest/set identity, required/current schema compatibility evidence, routing contract version, secret-file names/targets but never values, release timestamp/run ID, previous accepted release, and rollback eligibility. Application-only rollback must be false unless backward compatibility with the current schema identity is positively proved. No workflow may apply migrations automatically.
5. Extend the governed ed-new operator control plane with a narrowly allowlisted v3-app-deploy operation and, if useful, explicit v3-app-rollback/status operations. Request JSON may carry only a validated exact release_sha and other strictly necessary immutable identifiers. The workflow must checkout trusted main, prove the requested SHA is exactly the current accepted main head (or a specifically documented safer protected-head rule), build/test the images on the GitHub runner from frozen inputs, generate and validate the manifest, and transfer OCI image archives plus a sanitized runtime bundle over pinned SSH. Production must only docker load/pull immutable images, stage under an exact release directory, preserve existing host-only secrets, and run the reviewed Compose authority; no source checkout update, dependency install, build, registry-token leak, DB write, migration, wholesale V2 restore, or unrelated container restart. Keep action SHAs pinned and use the existing ed-new-operator environment/known-host trust.
6. Provide an idempotent host deploy script with a two-phase preflight/switch. Before switch: validate archive/manifest hashes, image content IDs, host, Docker/Compose, topology, secret presence/permissions, live schema identity via a read-only bounded mechanism, current app release and rollback compatibility. Stage without disrupting the current app. At switch: recreate only API and web/proxy, retain public-auth-edge and data/support containers, then positively verify container health, exact build SHA, origin/public /api/health shape, /openapi.json, anonymous /api/auth/session, presence of all current auth routes, root static shell, representative Svelte deep routes, static assets, API routing and numeric /s/{id64}. Commit the current-release pointer only after every check passes. On post-switch failure automatically restore the previous application release only when its manifest is eligible and schema-compatible; otherwise fail closed and emit a sanitized manual-recovery receipt.
7. Bootstrap existing app secrets only through a deliberate on-host, non-logging compatibility path if necessary. It may read the current API container environment locally and write an explicit allowlist into root-owned 0600 secret files without ever printing, uploading or embedding values; refuse ambiguous/missing/duplicate values and never overwrite an existing secret. Do not claim Frontier is configured if the old container lacks it. Keep this bootstrap separate from normal deploy and covered by tests. Prefer existing host secret files when discoverable.
8. Emit sanitized build/deploy/rollback receipts and upload the release manifest/receipt as short-retention Actions artifacts. Add exact regression tests for request-schema rejection, no secret output/literals, no production build/git pull, service allowlist, host guard, digest/SHA/schema validation, release-pointer atomicity, rollback fail-closed behaviour, nginx route ownership, Docker/Compose syntax, image provenance, API *_FILE resolution and health identity. Run focused Python tests, existing V3/decommission/operator contracts, apps/web check/lint/format/test/build, container builds, nginx -t, docker compose config with dummy secret paths/non-secret topology, Semgrep-compatible secret scans and git diff --check.

Do not deploy or access production from this worker, do not mutate DB/OAuth/Stage27, do not merge branches, and do not weaken the existing safe recovery scanner. Leave the branch ready for a focused PR into main and document the exact one-time operator sequence needed after the complete Svelte application head is merged.
